q: Popa's cocycle superrigidity theorem (2007) extends Zimmer's to non-linear targets. It states that for a Bernoulli action Γ ↷ (X^Γ,μ^Γ) of a group Γ with property (T) or a product group, any measurable cocycle α: Γ×X → Λ (target group Λ):
opts: Is cohomologous to a group homomorphism Γ → Λ (a 'virtual homomorphism')
Depends only on the group structure of Λ
exp: Popa's cocycle superrigidity: for Bernoulli actions of groups with property (T), every cocycle into a countable group (or an algebraic group) is cohomologous to a group homomorphism. This implies orbit equivalence implies conjugacy for many groups—a vast strengthening of Zimmer's theorem.
